label: hv-morph-allometry
topic: Scaling and allometry statements: Kleiber, surface-area/volume, Murray's law for vessels, limb scaling
summary:
Harvested 11 scaling statements, validated 4 against the AnAge mammal table, and wrote one Lean file that did NOT check.

**Validation (AnAge, mammals only, n=422, 2.4 g to 3.67 t, plain least squares on log10 values):**

| Statement | Prediction | Measured | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kleiber 3/4 law | slope 0.75 | 0.709, 95% CI [0.694, 0.725] | FAIL |
| Surface law 2/3 | slope 0.667 | same fit | FAIL |
| Curvature (not a pure power law) | upper-half slope > lower-half | 0.791 (se 0.015) vs 0.607 (se 0.027) | PASS |
| Mass-specific rate | slope -0.25 | -0.291 | FAIL (same data as row 1) |

The fit has no body-temperature or phylogeny correction, so the two failures are for the naive pooled form only. White & Seymour reached 2/3 only after those corrections.

**Lean:** `AllometryScaling.lean` has three theorems (Kleiber mass-specific form, cube surface-to-volume, Murray cube law from flow = k r^3 plus conservation), no sorry, no axioms. Both allowed check runs FAILED at `import Mathlib` with "failed to read file ... .olean.private" in the shared Mathlib cache, a different file each time. The first file named exists on disk, so this looks environmental (possibly memory or concurrent use), but that is not confirmed. Nothing is proved.

**Registry coverage:**
- **Kleiber:** no hit for "kleiber" in `lean/registry/laws`, `lean/laws.json`, `lean/LAWS.md`, `tracks/lean` or `tracks/research`.
- **Murray:** found only in `tracks/research` (`t3-lumen-law.json` and two bm-* agents), not in the Lean law registry.
- **Present by filename only (contents not opened):** `elastic-similarity`, `scaling-area-law`, `scaling-strength-law`, `scaling-bending-law`, `flight-allometry-law`, `disc-pectoral-length-allometry`.

**Sources not opened:** Kleiber 1932, Alexander 1979 and Savage 2004 were not found on Europe PMC; Murray 1926 and Stahl 1967 returned a title but no abstract. Findings resting on these are marked low confidence.

findings.claim: S1 Kleiber's law: basal metabolic rate B = a*M^(3/4). Formal: exists a>0 such that for all species, log B = log a + 0.75 log M + error, error mean zero. Assumptions: basal conditions, single pooled power law. Registry: NOT present (no 'kleiber' hit in lean registry or tracks). Falsifier: AnAge mammal rows, OLS slope of log10(W) on log10(g); reject if 95% CI excludes 0.75. VALIDATED: FAIL.
findings.source: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.276.5309.122 (statement of the law, abstract opened via Europe PMC); data https://genomics.senescence.info/species/dataset.zip
findings.value: predicted slope 0.75; measured 0.7091 (se 0.0079, 95% CI 0.6936-0.7246, n=422 mammals)
findings.evidence_quote: including the 3/4 power law for metabolic rates
findings.confidence: medium: the fit is my own naive OLS with no temperature or phylogeny correction; Kleiber's 1932 original was not opened

findings.claim: S2 Surface (geometric) law: mammalian BMR proportional to M^(2/3). Formal: slope b = 2/3 in log B = log a + b log M after correcting for body temperature, digestive state and phylogeny. Registry: not present as a metabolic law. Falsifier: same AnAge fit; reject if CI excludes 0.667. VALIDATED on uncorrected data: FAIL (measured slope lies between 2/3 and 3/4).
findings.evidence_quote: finds no support for a metabolic scaling exponent of 3/4
findings.confidence: medium: my test omits the corrections the paper says are needed, so this fails only the uncorrected form

findings.claim: S3 Curvature: log metabolic rate vs log mass is convex, so no single exponent holds. Formal: d^2(log B)/d(log M)^2 > 0; testable as slope(upper mass half) > slope(lower mass half). Registry: not present. Falsifier: AnAge mammals split at median mass; reject if upper slope <= lower slope. VALIDATED: PASS.
findings.value: lower-half slope 0.6065 (se 0.0267, n=211); upper-half slope 0.7909 (se 0.0151, n=211)
findings.evidence_quote: has convex curvature on a logarithmic scale, and is therefore not a pure power law
findings.confidence: medium-high: difference is about 6 standard errors, but a median split is a crude curvature test

findings.claim: S4 Mass-specific metabolic rate B/M = a*M^(-1/4) (algebraic consequence of S1; M>0). Registry: not present. Falsifier: slope of log(B/M) on log M in AnAge mammals; reject if CI excludes -0.25. VALIDATED: FAIL, same data as S1 so not independent.
findings.confidence: medium: the algebra is written in Lean but the Lean file did not check

findings.claim: S5 Murray's law: at a vessel branch, r0^3 = r1^3 + r2^3. Formal: if flow Q_i = k*r_i^3 with common k != 0 (minimum-work condition) and Q0 = Q1 + Q2, then r0^3 = r1^3 + r2^3. Registry: not in lean registry; 'murray' appears only in tracks/research (t3-lumen-law.json, bm-bioinspired-generative-design, bm-diffusion-kinetics). Falsifier: fit exponent x in r0^x = r1^x + r2^x on measured bifurcation radii; reject if CI excludes 3. Candidate dataset: published coronary arterial tree morphometry tables (not opened, not confirmed open).
findings.evidence_quote: cube of the radius of a parent vessel equals the sum of the cubes
findings.confidence: high for the statement; no dataset opened, so not validated. Murray 1926 (doi 10.1073/pnas.12.3.207) record found, title only, no abstract available

findings.claim: S6 West-Brown-Enquist model: 3/4 scaling follows from a space-filling fractal branching network, minimised energy dissipation and size-invariant terminal tubes. Formal: (space-filling) AND (dissipation minimised) AND (terminal tube size independent of M) implies B proportional to M^(3/4). Registry: not present. Falsifier: capillary dimensions vs body mass across mammals; reject the premise if terminal vessel radius scales with exponent significantly different from 0. Also indirectly failed by the curvature result S3.
findings.evidence_quote: the terminal tubes do not vary with body size
findings.confidence: high for the statement; no dataset opened for the premise test. Kolokotrones 2010 abstract says a vascular-architecture model fails the curvature test

findings.claim: S7 Elastic similarity: length scales as diameter^(2/3) in limbs and trunks. Formal: l = c*d^(2/3); with M proportional to l*d^2 this gives l proportional to M^(1/4), d proportional to M^(3/8). Registry: PRESENT by filename (lean/registry/laws/elastic-similarity.json; contents not opened). Falsifier: regress log bone length on log body mass; reject if CI excludes 0.25.
findings.evidence_quote: lengths increase as the (2/3) power of diameter
findings.confidence: high for the statement; the M^(1/4), M^(3/8) forms are my derivation from it

findings.claim: S8 Biological frequencies (heart rate, breathing rate) scale as M^(-1/4). Formal: f = c*M^(-1/4). Registry: not found. Falsifier: resting heart rate vs body mass across mammal species; reject if slope CI excludes -0.25. No open heart-rate table was opened in the time available.
findings.evidence_quote: biological frequencies are predicted to go inversely as body weight to the (1/4) power
findings.confidence: high for the statement; no dataset identified. Stahl 1967 (doi 10.1152/jappl.1967.22.3.453) record found, title only

findings.claim: S9 Body surface area scales as M^(5/8) under elastic similarity, versus M^(2/3) under geometric similarity. Formal: A = c*M^(0.625). Registry: scaling-area-law.json exists by filename (contents not opened; may be the 2/3 form). Falsifier: measured skin area vs mass; the two predictions differ by 0.042 in slope, so the test needs a standard error below about 0.02.
findings.evidence_quote: total body surface areas should correlate with body weight to the (5/8) power
findings.confidence: high for the statement; no dataset opened

findings.claim: S10 Geometric surface-to-volume law: for similar shapes, area proportional to L^2, volume to L^3, so S/V proportional to 1/L and S proportional to V^(2/3); for a cube S/V = 6/L. Registry: PRESENT by filename (scaling-area-law.json, thompson1917-ch02-* entries; contents not opened). Falsifier: pure geometry given the similarity assumption; the biological test is whether organisms are geometrically similar (see S7, S11).
findings.source: Elementary geometry; the registry attributes related entries to Thompson 1917 (not opened by me)
findings.confidence: high for the mathematics; primary source not opened

findings.claim: S11 Limb bone scaling across land mammals: reported exponents are close to geometric similarity (length about M^0.35) and not elastic similarity (M^0.25). Registry: scaling-bending-law.json and scaling-strength-law.json exist by filename (not opened). Falsifier: regress log limb bone length on log mass; elastic similarity rejected if CI excludes 0.25.
findings.source: Alexander et al. 1979, J. Zool. (doi 10.1111/j.1469-7998.1979.tb03964.x) - NOT OPENED, not found on Europe PMC
findings.confidence: low: the 0.35 figure is from memory and unverified; treat as a lead, not a finding

key_claims: In AnAge mammals (n=422) the pooled metabolic slope is 0.709, 95% CI 0.694-0.725: both 3/4 and 2/3 fall outside the interval on uncorrected data.
The slope rises from 0.61 in the lighter half of species to 0.79 in the heavier half, consistent with the published curvature finding.
Kleiber's law is absent from the Lean law registry and from tracks/lean and tracks/research; Murray's law appears only in tracks/research.
The Lean file did not check: both runs failed reading Mathlib cache files, so nothing is proved.

lay_summary: Bigger animals burn more energy, but not in step with their weight: an animal ten times heavier uses only about five times the energy.
Scientists have argued for a century about the exact rule, with one camp saying the power is three quarters and another saying two thirds.
We checked a public table of 422 mammal species and got a number in between (about 0.71), so on raw data neither tidy rule fits exactly.
The line also bends: small mammals follow a shallower rule than large ones, which matches what a 2010 study reported.
We also wrote three small maths proofs about these rules, but the proof checker could not load its library, so they do not count yet.

glossary.allometry: How a body feature changes as overall body size changes.
glossary.basal metabolic rate (BMR): The energy an animal uses per second while resting and not digesting.
glossary.exponent / power law: A rule of the form y = a times x raised to a fixed power; the power is the exponent.
glossary.slope (on a log-log plot): The exponent of a power law, read off as the steepness of a straight line after taking logarithms.
glossary.OLS (ordinary least squares): The standard way of fitting a straight line through scattered points.
glossary.95% confidence interval (CI): The range in which the true value plausibly lies given the data.
glossary.standard error (se): A measure of how uncertain a fitted number is.
glossary.Kleiber's law: The claim that metabolic rate goes as body mass to the 3/4 power.
glossary.surface law: The claim that metabolic rate goes as body mass to the 2/3 power, like skin area.
glossary.mass-specific rate: Energy use per gram of body.
glossary.convex curvature: The line bends upward instead of staying straight.
glossary.Murray's law: At a fork in a blood vessel, the parent radius cubed equals the sum of the branch radii cubed.
glossary.geometric similarity: Big and small animals having the same shape, just scaled up.
glossary.elastic similarity: The idea that bones and trunks get relatively thicker with size so they bend equally under their own weight.
glossary.space-filling fractal network: A branching system of tubes that repeats the same pattern at smaller sizes and reaches every part of the body.
glossary.phylogeny: The family tree of species; related species are not independent data points.
glossary.Lean / Mathlib: A computer program that checks mathematical proofs, and its standard library.
glossary.olean: A compiled library file that Lean must load before checking a proof.
glossary.falsifier: A test whose outcome could show the statement is wrong.

recommendations: Add Kleiber's law, the 2/3 surface law and the curvature statement to the registry as three competing entries with the AnAge mammal test attached; the naive fit already separates them.
Repeat the fit with body-temperature and phylogenetic correction before recording any final verdict on 2/3 versus 3/4.
Rerun check.sh on AllometryScaling.lean when the machine is quiet; if the 'failed to read file' error persists, inspect the shared Mathlib cache at C:\Temp\delphi-lean-lake.
Promote Murray's law from tracks/research into the Lean registry once a bifurcation radius table is located for the exponent test.
Open Alexander 1979 before using the limb-bone exponent; it is unverified here.
